newsitem.title: USA: USDA April 11 U.S. crop highlights -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: USDA April 11 U.S. crop highlights -- USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday slashed U.S. soybean ending stocks for 1996/97 to 125 million bushels, citing lower than expected March 1 soybean stocks, and higher seed use and other residual use.
The drop was much larger than expected by market analysts.

In its April supply/demand report, USDA dropped soybean exports to 895 million bushels. It said rising prices and a forecast cut in imports by Taiwan are expected to cut the pace of U.S. soybean exports. USDA lifted its U.S. soybean imports forecast to 5 million bushels from 4 million. It left the soybean crush at a record 1.42 billion bushels.

USDA lowered its forecast for U.S. corn ending stocks to 909 million bushels, and dropped corn exports to 1.825 billion. It lowered wheat ending stocks to 460 million bushels, but forecast that exports would rise by 35 million bushels to 985 million due to stronger than expected late-season sales.
USDA also lifted its wheat imports forecast by 10 million bushels to 90 million, citing a surge in imports from Canada. Analysts had forecast corn and wheat ending stocks to dip.
U.S. 1996/97 cotton exports were pegged at 7.00 million bales, up 20,000 bales, and ending stocks were lowered to 3.95 million bales from the previous month's 4.15 million.
